title: Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion
status_note: Published Jan. 15, 2025; created ECCN 4E091 for certain closed model weights. Rescinded by BIS in May 2025 and never enforced. NOT currently operative law. Remains precedential as evidence of the control design an agency believed ECRA authorized, and its reasoning survives the repeal.
passages: The rule established ECCN 4E091 covering model weights of certain advanced closed-weight artificial intelligence models, and imposed a worldwide licensing framework allocating compute capacity by country tier.
Model weights of open-weight models published to the public were not controlled under 4E091; the control reached closed weights whose holder had not published them.
The framework was rescinded before any enforcement action was taken under it.

title: Published information and software
status_note: Currently operative provision of the Export Administration Regulations.
passages: Information is published, and so is not subject to the EAR, when it has been made available to the public without restrictions upon its further dissemination.

Publication includes availability through libraries open to the public, through unlimited distribution at a conference or meeting open to the public, and through posting on the Internet where it may be accessed by any interested party.
The published exclusion has historically performed constitutional-avoidance work, keeping the export control regime clear of ordinary scientific publication.

title: Export Control Reform Act of 2018
status_note: Enacted as part of Pub. L. No. 115-232; permanent statutory authority for the Export Administration Regulations.
passages: The Act authorizes the President to control the export, reexport, and in-country transfer of items subject to the jurisdiction of the United States, including dual-use items, to the extent necessary for national security and foreign policy.
The Act directs a regular process to identify emerging and foundational technologies essential to national security that are not already subject to control.
The Act does not by its terms name software model parameters, and its breadth is the subject of both the government's authority argument and the major-questions counterargument.

title: International Emergency Economic Powers Act - informational materials exception (Berman Amendment)
status_note: Berman Amendment exception to IEEPA authority; currently operative.
passages: The authority granted to the President under this section does not include the authority to regulate or prohibit, directly or indirectly, the importation or exportation of information or informational materials.
The exception enumerates categories including publications, films, artworks, and CD ROMs, and applies regardless of format or medium of transmission.
Whether trained model weights fall within informational materials is contested and is the operative question for an IEEPA-based restriction.

title: Export - release of technology or source code to a foreign person in the United States
status_note: Currently operative deemed-export provision of the EAR.
passages: Release of technology or source code subject to the EAR to a foreign person in the United States is deemed to be an export to the foreign person's most recent country of citizenship or permanent residency.
A deemed export may require a license even though no item physically leaves the United States.
The provision is the mechanism by which a control on model artifacts would reach foreign graduate students working in a United States university laboratory.

title: National Policy on the Transfer of Scientific, Technical and Engineering Information
status_note: Issued Sept. 21, 1985; repeatedly reaffirmed as standing federal policy. Executive policy, not a statute or regulation, and therefore persuasive rather than binding on a court.
passages: It is the policy of this Administration that, to the maximum extent possible, the products of fundamental research remain unrestricted.
Fundamental research means basic and applied research in science and engineering, the results of which ordinarily are published and shared broadly within the scientific community.
Where national security requires control, the mechanism for control of information generated during federally funded fundamental research is classification.

title: Administrative Procedure Act - scope of review
status_note: Currently operative standard of review for agency action.
passages: The reviewing court shall hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law.
The reviewing court shall also hold unlawful and set aside agency action found to be contrary to constitutional right, power, privilege, or immunity.
Arbitrary-and-capricious review of a rulemaking record interacts with the constitutional avoidance canon where the agency's chosen reading raises a serious First Amendment question.
